title: The docs repo: schema, style, and an honest first seed of what is actually known
done: Created linux-phone-oco/docs from text-as-data-template. Schema: devices, components, support_status (the matrix), device_sources, plus the template's backlog/session_log/sources. Adopted software-engineering-canon's RFC-like Jekyll theme verbatim (monospace, uniform heading size, definition-list field/value rendering, 72-character width) rather than inventing a new one, since it already does exactly what was asked for and is proven. Seeded one device (xiaomi-surya) and 19 components with status, citing only what was actually confirmed by search earlier in the session; everything not confirmed is marked unknown rather than guessed.
considered: Reusing ideal-project-playbook's concepts/relations schema for this too.
rejected: Concepts/relations model general, reusable PRINCIPLES with their relationships; a hardware support matrix is a different shape (a fact about one device and one component, not a principle), and forcing it into that model would be more awkward than a purpose-built pair of tables.

title: The phone, for real: bootloader unlocked, product confirmed, two jobs run end to end
done: Ran the first two real jobs through lab-agent against the physical device: a read-only USB probe (0001, phone not connected at the time) and fastboot getvar all (0002, phone connected). Confirmed for real: product=surya (matches the docs repo's device id), unlocked=yes, kernel=uefi, secure=yes, serial fcbd04b4, and the full stock Android partition layout. Cross-checked against upstream: this device migrated from per-device pmaports packages to the generic qcom-sm7150 port (U-Boot + systemd-boot + EFI, March 2025), which changes the install/partition steps from the older device-specific instructions - U-Boot goes to boot, the pmOS boot image to cache, the rootfs to userdata.
considered: Attempting a fastboot boot or flash as part of this same session.
rejected: The user mentioned the device already has something called 'nuria' installed or flashed, which does not match any term found in the sm7150-mainline/postmarketOS sources searched; flashing or booting anything before that is understood risks overwriting or being inconsistent with whatever is actually there.

title: The distro is Nura now: postmarketOS renamed in September
done: Verified via search (the project's own governance document pmcr 0003, endoflife.date, and independent coverage in several languages): postmarketOS officially renamed to Nura on 2026-09-27, a post-cutoff event. Updated this repo's own prose (devices.notes, two support_status.notes) to say Nura, formerly postmarketOS, on first mention. Left untouched: source titles (they quote real external documents, written before the rename, under their real titles), and tool/package names (pmaports, pmbootstrap, the postmarketos.org and gitlab.postmarketos.org domains) - the rename announcement itself says those stay as-is while the transition completes, so rewriting them would be guessing at URLs and package names that may not have moved yet.
considered: Rewriting every mention of postmarketOS throughout, including source titles and URLs.
rejected: A source's title is a citation of a real document; it is not this repository's to edit, renamed project or not. Guessing at new URLs for domains the announcement itself says are still valid would trade a working link for an unverified one.

title: Nura boots and is reachable on the network; no shell access without credentials
done: Rebooted the phone out of fastboot (job 0003): it is Nura, not Android, so adb does not apply at all - the real access method is SSH over a USB network interface fixed at 172.16.42.1. Confirmed (job 0004): the interface comes up and 172.16.42.1 answers ping in about 3ms, so the boot itself genuinely succeeds. Port 22 (SSH) refuses connections. Checked (job 0005) whether that meant an encrypted root filesystem waiting at a telnet unlock prompt, the standard pmOS/Nura pattern - port 23 is also refused outright, not just silent, which rules out the simple disk-unlock explanation and means neither service is enabled on this particular install.
considered: Trying common default usernames or passwords to get a shell.
rejected: Guessing credentials against a real device is not something to do unilaterally, security concerns aside from whether it would even work; the honest and correct move is to ask whoever configured this install.

title: A fresh-install plan, prepared but not run: two things only the owner can answer
done: With no shell access to the existing install, the alternative is a clean reinstall. Found the pieces: U-Boot release 2025-12-02 (github.com/sm7150-mainline/u-boot), a Nura/pmOS edge build at images.postmarketos.org/bpo/edge/qcom-sm7150/, and the documented partition steps (U-Boot to boot, the decompressed boot image to cache, the rootfs to userdata). Two things block actually running it, both things only the device's owner can answer, not things to guess: (1) which panel variant this specific unit has, Huaxing or Tianma - the official wiki's own method needs adb logcat while booted into stock Android, which this phone no longer has, and picking wrong means a blank screen until reflashed with the other one; (2) whether to proceed with a destructive reinstall at all, given the existing install cannot be examined first.
considered: Guessing the panel variant (roughly even odds) to save a round trip.
rejected: Wrong is not catastrophic here (reflash fixes it) but is still avoidable, and pmbootstrap asks the installer to choose this explicitly, so the owner may simply already know which one was chosen.

title: Boot hang found; ADSP crash loop found; lab-agent hardened
done: Audited the WCD937x patch on the lab machine (no IRQ collisions, no MMIO overlaps); proved on hardware that aoncc caused the boot hang; got SSH over USB on first boot (a preset beats Nura disable-sshd preset); found the ADSP crash loop and traced it to the sensor registry in hexagonrpcd. lab-agent: agent API, durable results, local-first monitor, GitHub budget fixes, ntfy notifications; surya-lab repo with DT audit and flash tools.
considered: Interrupt collisions and missing LPASS votes as the hang cause (refuted or unsupported by the audits).
rejected: A Python API for agents (the CLI with stable JSON is the API); a second monitor command (one command chooses local or remote).

title: Stereo speakers, shells, the grand picture, the device lab
done: Speaker stereo on surya (tas2562 slot-length fix + stereo UCM), verified by ear through PipeWire on Sxmo, Phosh and Plasma. Plasma: a saved mixer state and a tas2562 volume bug silenced the amps; found and recorded. The grand picture: tad-engine draws matrices, a 46-feature catalog against Android, iOS and Linux, the device grid, an automatic test suite whose runs are filed here, weekly feeds (the postmarketOS wiki claims, kernel work on surya), the research sorted into the orgs. The device lab: flash with the fixes built in, provisioning (packages, Wi-Fi), one phone library, an Sxmo device profile.
considered: Separate boards per project (labels on tasks chosen: one source of truth); a PR from the feed workflow (the org forbids it: verified data is committed instead); loosening the org policy for one feed.
rejected: Guessing statuses for the Linux distributions (left unknown until tests and feeds fill them); PC-side depmod when baking in a module (it made Plasma boot-loop); trusting an image by its folder name (a reference image carried an old test device tree - fingerprints now).

title: The conveyor in Rust, health that watches itself, the microphone narrowed
done: devlab in lab-tools, for any phone from its manifest: reaching the phone, the safe test-kernel try (boot counting, a timeout that falls back to stock, proven live), provision, test, health and watch (a regression against everything that ever passed raises one board task; silent when well). Sound silently lost to Sxmo's loopback card as the default output: fixed by the speaker's UCM priority, and now a check. The tas2562 volume fixed (0 dB had muted the amps). sxmo-deviceprofiles repo. Board: states at a glance, waits that show themselves, mouse selection, real editing in the reply box.
considered: Retrying the WCD test kernel with more variations; GitHub auto-merge for releases (a workflow token's merge starts no workflows); the initramfs debug shell for unattended tries.
rejected: The clocks as the WCD cause (pinned on: same failure); the reset pin's mux as the cause (fixed: same failure); boot-time dyndbg for module code (it reaches only built-in code); dmesg for crash counts (a ring overwritten within minutes - the journal is complete).

title: The project's own data in Russian
done: A translations table (ocoeco SPEC section 9) with this project's own feature names and categories, device parts and milestones in Russian, every row marked by machine until a person reviews it; exported through the mark, so the observatory's Russian pages read them.
considered: Translated columns inside the source tables.
rejected: That: translations never change the source; and nobody else translates this project's data.

title: The first real devlab flash, and what a clean flash exposed
done: surya flashed from the pristine stock image by devlab flash (device tree a43d069d0a49adcd, the manifest's fixes baked in) and brought back by devlab provision: 102 GB, Firefox, the Sxmo profile, Wi-Fi, 20 of 20 checks. Two first-boot faults became the tool's job (a clock at the image's build date; a filesystem left at 2 GB on a 104 GB partition) with a new check. Then the health watch caught the audio DSP crashing on every resume - rare before the flash - which makes the old suspend crash reproducible and shows the manifest lacks a change the old system had.
considered: Treating the crashes as damage from the flash.
rejected: That: the phone's own log showed the idle suspend as the trigger; nothing was changed until the log was read.

title: Linux Phones tells its essence
done: Its idea written for anyone - the phone you own and do not control, a conveyor and an honest picture - and its workings: what delivers and proves each step of the paths of Linux Phones and of surya, with why we care. Three first steps of Linux Phones are left with nothing under them: nothing yet measures calls, connectivity or the daily basics on the best current Linux phone.
considered: Filling every step with something.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves should stand empty and be seen.

title: What the ear heard is withdrawn

considered: Keeping the claim with a caveat.
rejected: That: evidence from an instrument that moves is not evidence.

title: Four of surya's parts no longer unknown
done: The phone's own checks were widened and its parts follow their evidence: Wi-Fi works (joined, gateway answers); Bluetooth partly (powered, hears devices; pairing untried); sensors and the fingerprint reader broken (nothing exposed - the sensor service is masked because it crashed the audio processor). Calls and messages stay unknown for a plain reason now written down: there is no SIM card in the phone. The cameras' fault is narrowed: the pipeline is there, no image sensor is bound.

rejected: That: a part works when its function was shown, not when its device appears.

title: The ear in health
done: devlab health --hear listens as part of health: heard checks join the one baseline and regress like any other. The rule made honest rather than a second baseline: a run that did not listen is out of scope for what only listening tells. The watcher never makes a sound by itself.

done: surya flashed from the pristine stock image by devlab flash and brought back by devlab provision, all 20 checks passing; flash.sh removed, as planned once devlab had done a real flash. A new check, root-fills-its-partition: the first boot had left the system at 2 GB on a 104 GB partition.

title: Both speakers heard - then withdrawn
done: With the author's EarPods as the lab's microphone, devlab hear played a 1000 Hz tone on each speaker and heard both: left at -24.0 dBFS, right at -29.2 dBFS, each over 70 dB above the silent room. WITHDRAWN the same day: the microphone was worn by the author and moved; neither the levels nor the 5 dB difference can be relied on.

rejected: That, on one measurement from one position.

title: The lab's idea, told for anyone
done: What this lab is - one particular phone, everything true of it written down, experiments that fall back by themselves - as a piece of writing for a reader who knows nothing of it.
rejected: A list of files.

title: The suspend crash found: a FastRPC helper attached at suspend
done: After the flash the audio DSP died on every suspend attempt (the attempts abort at once: the USB link cannot go idle). Found by experiment, one change at a time: not a first-boot effect (9 of 9 on the second boot), not the sensor proxy (15 of 15 without it), but hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper - 0 of 8 without it, and 0 of 9 on a clean boot with it masked, all 21 checks passing. Masked in the manifest, so every flash has it. The check's resume counter, which always said 0, rewritten in awk and checked against a boot with 24.
considered: A hand-made change the manifest lacked; a first-boot effect; the sensor proxy; a stream left open.
rejected: All four, each by its own measurement. The old 'rare' crash was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down.

title: What the ear heard is withdrawn
done: The microphone was the author's earphones, worn on his head: its distance from the phone changed as he moved. The levels measured, the difference seen between the two speakers, and the passes themselves cannot be relied on. The heard checks are out of the baseline and the lab's microphone is un-named until one is fixed in place; the tool stays, proven to work mechanically.
considered: Keeping the results with a caveat.
rejected: That: evidence from an instrument that moves is not evidence, and a later failure would have looked like the phone getting worse.

title: The USB link no longer flaps
done: Reported by the author: the phone kept reconnecting on his PC (26 USB disconnects in 5 minutes on the lab machine). On USB a suspend cannot complete, and the shell retried every 12 seconds, each attempt dropping the link. A small service holds a kernel wake lock while the port is connected to a host - independent of any shell - baked in by the manifest, with a check. Known before, never written down: it is now.
considered: Changing the shell's suspend hook.
rejected: That: a fix inside one shell does not hold under another, or under none.

title: More of the phone, measured
done: Eight of the phone's twenty parts stood as unknown. The checks now also ask: is Wi-Fi joined and does the gateway answer; is Bluetooth powered and does it hear anything; is there a SIM and is the modem ready; does the kernel expose a headset-jack detector, a fingerprint reader, any motion or light sensor, any image sensor behind the camera pipeline. All read-only.
considered: Marking parts as working from a device node alone.
rejected: That: there and set up is what a machine can prove; the rest are witnessed tests.

title: The port table cleared; a boot spent on a missing tool
done: The TX bus's port layout and timings match mainline sm8250 and the vendor's layout for the ports in use - not the cause. A boot to dump the SoundWire registers found this kernel has no SoundWire debugfs.
considered: Seven ports against the vendor's five as the cause.
rejected: That, after comparing the ports actually used. And booting before checking the tool exists - a lesson: check the instrument first.

title: Why the cameras are dark, and the way in
done: Read from the phone and from sources, changing nothing: the camera pipeline and its control buses work; the phone's description lists no sensor. The vendor's kernel yields the wiring of seven sensor slots but no model names. Written up with the wiring table and a four-step way in (research/cameras.md).
considered: Describing the sensors from the models reported for this phone elsewhere.
rejected: That: hearsay. A chip should say what it is, on its own bus, before a driver is bound to it.

title: The microphone codec comes up
done: Traced the codec's timeout to a bus clash on the microphone-side SoundWire bus, and that to one pin muxed to the wrong function in the audio pin driver (and one more on the receive side), read against the phone's own Android kernel. Corrected and rebuilt: the codec initialises and the sound card is made with it. Recording through it is next.
considered: The macros' autosuspend; the upstream revert (it gives no reason).
rejected: Guessing at clock fixes.

title: The microphone's chain, nearly whole
done: Booted the microphone test kernel (after finding the earlier tries had been given a gzip kernel): for the first time everything up to the codec came up; the card fails on one timeout. Measured which speaker is the bottom one. Saw a boot with no sound card and recorded it.
considered: Theories about the bootloader.
rejected: Acting before reading the bootloader's own record.

done: The SIM is seen and ready (1&1). The modem stays shutting-down and refuses to go online, even after a reboot; it loops on one file through tqftpserv, ending each read itself. One theory - a missing read-write directory - was checked and is wrong: the directory exists.
considered: A missing directory.
rejected: That: the program's own paths showed it exists.

done: Listed the codec's recording side in the test kernel and read how the phone's own Android build routes its main microphone; the names match closely. Found that the kernel branch's pin driver differs from the tested tree - the fix is to be ported, not pasted.
considered: Pasting the table change into the branch.
rejected: That: the branch's driver is not the one that was tested.

done: The main-microphone route from the phone's Android build sets cleanly in the test kernel; the capture stream fails when it starts - the TX bus loses the codec exactly when it is reshaped for the stream. Ruled out power management. Measured the audio processor's once-a-second handover signal.
considered: Keeping the bus awake.
rejected: That as the answer: it changed nothing.

title: Telegram at provisioning: telegram-desktop, held by Alpine v3.24
done: The author asked for a Telegram client at provisioning as firefox is. Alpine ships one Telegram client for aarch64, the official telegram-desktop (no tdlib, no libpurple Telegram plugin for chatty, no Kotatogram); it went into provision/packages.txt (surya-lab #108). Installing it on the phone failed: v3.24 community ships 6.8.5-r0 linked to libada.so.3 while ada is now 4.0, so apk cannot resolve it even after apk update. devlab provision installs the list in one apk add, so the line would have failed firefox and i2c-tools too; it now waits there as a comment (surya-lab fix right after #108). Edge has 7.4.4-r0 rebuilt against libada.so.4. Nothing was installed or changed on the phone.
considered: Installing telegram-desktop from the edge repository for one package: it would pull edge libraries into a v3.24 system that another session is testing audio on.
rejected: chatty with a Telegram plugin: no such plugin is packaged. Keeping the line live: it breaks the whole package list.

title: Research: calls proven by an echo call, and how the health suites are organised
done: Read the phone (read only): the modem is online on LTE, Vodafone.de, data attached; q6voiced and callaudiod installed; no voice PCM in the kernel. Found one attested German echo line (blueSIP 99701) and its tone line (99702); read pulpoff/linux-surya's call path; designed the echo-call check and the data budget; surveyed the suites (shell checks with awk Goertzels, the tone crate never on the phone, no Rust toolchain on the phone, cargo script still nightly). Decided 2026-11-17-calls-proven-by-echo-call and 2026-11-17-health-checks-shell-and-rust; backlog calls-q6voice-kernel to calls-echo-check, health-data-check, health-analysis-in-rust, health-coverage-query; wrote surya-lab's failing check call-audio-path.
considered: A digital loop through in-call record ports; a two-phone stand; a programmable number; rust-script on the phone; every check in Rust.

The proven microphone-only kernel (pmos-mic, 7.1.0-sm7150-mic+) is still installed as a fallback; stock (7.1.0-rc3-sm7150) boots after 3 bad boots. The old /lib/modules/7.1.0-rc3-sm7150-wcd belongs to a removed experiment and can go. HEALTHY: the last runs say healthy, 37-39 pass, 4 known gaps (fingerprint, sensors, both cameras). WORKS, proven by the phone itself: speakers (stereo), earpiece (= the top TAS2564 speaker; the WCD9375 EAR amplifier is silent), both microphones (bottom ADC1, top ADC2 at INP3) through the UCM profile, mobile data (Vodafone.de LTE; tqftpserv 1.3 from Alpine edge, a gsm connection with no APN), SMS (texts its own number, telephony layer, daily), calls both ways (q6voice, Voice Call UCM verb, q6voiced on PCM 0,6, devlab-call-uplink, daily call-echo to blueSIP's echo line +49 89 721010 99701 - its announcement lasts ~19 s). MUST NOT BE UNDONE: the VoiceMMode1 TX Topology 69488 set in the HiFi verb at boot (the DSP builds its voice processor once, at the first call of a boot; a call set up with the default 0x10F71 keeps the uplink silent until a reboot); the codec node has no sleep pin state (ASoC holds it in reset otherwise); /etc/modprobe.d/devlab-pd-mapper.conf (loads qcom_pd_mapper before the ADSP; without it ~1 boot in 5 has no sound card); tqftpserv@edge (1.1.1 keeps the modem in shutting-down); the SIM's own number lives only in ~/.config/devlab/xiaomi-surya/own-number and /etc/devlab/private/own-number - never in a repository. Test sounds are -6 dBFS at 20% (the author: soft). The SIM is in slot 2 (slot 1: no ATR). Never read /sys/kernel/debug/gpio or the LPI pinctrl at 62b40000 (manifest hazards).
considered: next: (1) headphones and the headset mic: need a headset plugged in and the author listening (verify-headphone-mic-earpiece; the jack detector exists since the WCD fixes). (2) upstream, waiting for the author to send: upstream-queue linux/sm7150-wcd 0001-0004 (sm7150-mainline), the tas2562 pair, upstream-alpine-tqftpserv, upstream-pd-mapper-order; q6voice is out of tree (sdm845-mainline) - its upstreaming is not ours yet. (3) the kernel is not yet a package: the kept kernel lives only on the phone's boot partition; a reflash returns stock until it goes through the package conveyor (device.toml carries the userspace side: UCM, q6voiced conf, call-uplink, pd-mapper, tqftpserv@edge, the mobile connection).
